results.reasoning: Judged headless (the rule's screen is a terminal moment; no server or port used) on throwaway machines built with tools/cli-scenarios.mjs machine() and fixture g2-undrawn-screens, running the working tree's lib/lint.js. Lint names cart as having no design and no open design request, says a proposed version counts only once a request's proposes: names it, and now prints `walkdown threads new --screen cart --reason request --body "<what the screen must show>" --blueprint 0001-sp-checkout`: the screen's real id, --reason request, a body placeholder and the registered blueprint id. I extracted that command from lint's own output, replaced only the placeholder, and ran it: it exited 0 and filed n-0002, a note with reason request anchored to screen cart, and the next lint reads 0 warnings. The same command run from /private/tmp, outside the project, files too, since the blueprint travels in the flag. A note with reason finding on cart leaves the warning standing; a request clears it; a version dropped in designs/cart/ with no request leaves it standing; a retired cart is not linted for it (lint says one retired screen was not linted; the remaining error is a different check about a rule naming the retired screen). The ended-thread step I read in code rather than drove, because only verified or waived end a request through the CLI and this judging writes neither: isLiveRequest in lib/vocab.js excludes TERMINAL statuses, and the hint change does not touch it. Edges: running the printed command without filling the body is accepted and files a request whose body is the literal placeholder, which clears the warning (estimated 10-20%, reported to the dispatching agent, not filed). A blueprint with no registry row would print --blueprint <id>, but under ADR 0003 lint only reaches registered blueprints (under 5%). A body a person fills with a double quote or $ needs ordinary shell escaping (under 10%).
